study type: Descriptive, transversal, analytical, and retrospective review
outcome: Maternal mortality due to obstetric hemorrhage
cohort: 51 patients who underwent obstetric hysterectomy between January 2012 and November 2015 at the General Hospital Dr. Aurelio Valdivieso in Oaxaca, Mexico.
finding: The study found a decreasing incidence of obstetric hysterectomy over the 4-year period, with the main indications being abnormal placental adhesion and uterine atony, and no maternal mortality due to obstetric hemorrhage.
